text:
Predicates:
RegisterToVoteUS(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
Participate2024(x) ::: x can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
CitizenUS(x) ::: x has United States citizenship.
CitizenTaiwanese(x) ::: x has Taiwanese citizenship.
OfficialRF(x) ::: x is a Russian Federation official.
ManagerGazprom(x) ::: x is a manager at Gazprom.
Premises:
∀x (RegisterToVoteUS(x) → Participate2024(x)) ::: Everyone who can register to vote in the United States can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
∀x (CitizenUS(x) → RegisterToVoteUS(x)) ::: If someone has United States citizenship, then they can register to vote in the United States.
∀x (CitizenUS(x) ⊕ CitizenTaiwanese(x)) ::: A person either has United States citizenship or Taiwanese citizenship.
∀x (OfficialRF(x) → ¬CitizenTaiwanese(x)) ::: No Russian Federation officials hold Taiwanese citizenship.
¬CitizenTaiwanese(vladimir) ∧ ¬ManagerGazprom(vladimir) ::: Vladimir neither holds Taiwanese citizenship nor is he a manager at Gazprom.
RegisterToVoteUS(ekaterina) ⊕ OfficialRF(ekaterina) ::: Ekaterina can register to vote in the United States, or she is a Russian Federation official.
Conclusion:
¬(RegisterToVoteUS(ekaterina) ∧ Participate2024(vladimir)) ::: It is not true that Ekaterina can register to vote in the United States and Vladimir can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
